newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

NSW Treasurer Michael Egan has presented a discussion paper to the state's electricity unions outlining a push to privatise the State's electricity industry. Under the proposal, A$22 billion would be raised for New South Wales, a figure that would eliminate its A$13.2 billion Budget sector debt. Page 1.

Taxation Commissioner Michael Carmody said yesterday more than 150,000 taxpayers and their tax agents will be targeted by the Australian Taxation Office in major crackdowns on rental property investors and those who split their incomes with family members through trusts, companies and partnerships. Page 3.

A by-election to be held tomorrow in the Queensland Labor seat of Kurwongbah will be the first electoral test for Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge since the Wik debate and the Pauline Hanson race debate. While most predict the election will return the Labor member, both Borbidge and Opposition Leader Peter Beattie are playing the underdog. Page 3.

Under changes recommended by a committee on electoral matters consisting of both Coalition and ALP members, political donations up to A$1,500 will be tax deductible. The committee report will be tabled in Parliament on June 16. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday rejected the view that immigration creates jobs, an opinion criticised by business groups and two state premiers. Howard also continued his attack on Independent MP Pauline Hanson, ridiculing her attempt to take credit for the slashing of the immigration intake. Page 1.

Following a death threat phoned to a Sydney courtroom on Wednesday, current affairs star Jana Wendt decided to accept a A$1.2 million out of court settlement from Channel 7. The settlement was well below the A$6.4 million compensation Wendt was after. Seven claims she feared being cross-examined. Page 1.

New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan has sparked great debate, last night releasing a blueprint for the full privatisation of the state's A$22 billion power industry. Egan said the privatisation of the electricity industry would see New South Wales enter the 21st Century debt-free. Page 1.

On a video to be released today, Bernard Whelan, whose wife Kerry was kidnapped at the beginning of the month, has begged for her safe release, revealing that his three children were barely able to cope with the trauma. The plea comes as the Australian Bureau of Criminal Intelligence joins the New South Wales Police in a search for the kidnappers. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan has been backed by his Premier Bob Carr in his move to sell the state's electric industry to ensure New South Wales is debt-free. The A$22 billion sale would provide A$2 billion for investment, create a A$3 billion fund to rebuild infrastructure and improve the budget bottom line by A$500 million a year. Page 1.

The National Heart Foundation has released details of a seven-year, A$27 million study that suggests drug treatment to lower cholesterol would benefit thousands of heart disease patients who in the past have not been considered suitable for it. The study found that lowering average cholesterol levels in people with heart disease reduced overall death rates. Page 1.

In a video-taped appeal, Bernard Whelan, whose wife Kerry was kidnapped 17 days ago, has appealed to his wife's abductors to release her safely to their three "very vulnerable and barely coping" children. Police hope the appeal, which will be made public this morning, will help them find Mrs Whelan. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday defended Cabinet's decision to cut immigration, saying the move was not in response to calls from Pauline Hanson. Howard said that as far back as 1991 he believed there was a direct link between unemployment and immigation, and he added that the cut was in the national interest. Page 1.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard has attacked Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett over his criticism of the Federal Government's immigration cuts, and over the Victorian Government's imposing of some of the highest taxes of any state. Howard's comments come after Kennett claimed credit for forcing the Federal Government to move on tax reform. Page 1.

Victorian Community Services Minister Denis Napthine, former Health Minister Marie Tehan's parliamentary secretary, yesterday distanced himself from questions over the Intergraph memo affair. Questions emerged after it was revealed Napthine may have had knowledge of the sensitive documents. Page 1.

Paul Taga, 15, was shot in the back late on Wednesday night as he walked home along Fairbairn Road in Sunshine, after an alleged altercation with Anthony Frederick Fowler, 28, who was being held in police custody last night. It is believed Fowler shot Paul from his car. Page 1.

Qantas Airways will spend A$320 million installing interactive video screens on each of its seats that will offer movies, video games, and, if permission is granted, gaming functions. Other airlines, including British Airways and Swissair, are already exerimenting with in-flight gaming operations. Page 1.
